newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends up, soars to highs on close.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends up, soars to highs on close.

text.p: A late-session bout of speculative buying fueled CSCE world sugar futures sharply higher by the close, trading sources said.
The market recorded early gains amid trade buying and a dearth of selling, and then lingered around its intraday high at 10.44 cents basis July.
A move over 10.45 cents late in the day attracted buying by the speculators, who have remained steady sellers for the past two weeks.
July climbed to 11.50 cents, its highest level since reaching 11.54 cents on June 6. October hit a lifetime high of 11.35 cents, before easing slightly by the close.

The July contract settled 0.23 cent firmer at 11.49 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.24 to 11.50 cents. October ended up 0.19 cent at 11.34 cents, while the back months finished 0.14 and 0.13 higher.
"The market was chased up by the trade and once we got over 11.45 cents (July) and 11.30 cents (October), the speculators took over," a broker said.
While the speculators maintain a heavy net long position in the front month, they have plenty of time to liquidate positions with 11 trading days remaining before expiry, floor sources said.
As of early Wednesday, open interest in July stood at 72,995 lots, down 2,257 lots.
Liquidation should pick up after July options go out on Friday. Market sources said the July expiry should remain orderly, as the trade has been a steady buyer for the past couple of weeks.
"It looked like a raging bull market (today) but I dont think we'll see a gap down where the funds start dumping, and trade backs away," Merrill Lynch broker Tony Passimenti, said.
An estimated 31,016 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Wednesday's official 24,887 lots.
